javaExecution.title: Java Execution Pipeline & JDK/JRE/JVM Architecture
javaExecution.subtitle: Visualize Java source compilation (javac), ClassLoader Parent Delegation, Bytecode verification, and Execution Engine (Interpreter + JIT).
javaExecution.mentalModel: Java code follows 'Write Once, Run Anywhere' (WORA). Javac translates high-level Java into bytecode (.class), which JVM loads via ClassLoaders, verifies for safety, and compiles hot paths to native machine code via JIT.

failureModes: ClassNotFoundException vs NoClassDefFoundError: ClassNotFoundException occurs at runtime when dynamic loading (Class.forName) fails. NoClassDefFoundError occurs when a class was present during compilation but missing at runtime execution.
tradeOffs: JIT Warmup Overhead vs Native Speed: JIT compilation produces highly optimized native machine code for hot paths, but introduces initial warmup latency compared to Ahead-Of-Time (AOT) GraalVM native images.
theoryData.productionScenario: An SDE-2 backend service experienced 5-second latency spikes upon startup under heavy traffic. Investigating JVM flags revealed JIT TieredCompilation was warming up method call counters. Tuning `-XX:CompileThreshold=10000` and pre-warming endpoints eliminated startup latency spikes.

interviewQA.q: Explain the ClassLoader Parent Delegation Model in Java.
interviewQA.a: When a ClassLoader receives a request to load a class, it delegates the request up to its parent ClassLoader first before attempting to load the class itself. This prevents untrusted code from overriding core Java API classes like java.lang.Object.

quizData.question: Which ClassLoader is responsible for loading core Java runtime classes like java.lang.String?
quizData.answer: Bootstrap ClassLoader (written in C/C++ native code).

quizData.question: What is the primary role of the JIT (Just-In-Time) Compiler in the JVM?
quizData.answer: To compile frequently executed bytecode (hotspots) into native CPU machine code to achieve high runtime performance.
